items.stem: The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 requires what of employers and of places open to the public?
items.stemEs: La Ley de Estadounidenses con Discapacidades de 1990 exige ¿qué a los empleadores y a los lugares abiertos al público?

choices.text: Separate programmes and separate facilities designed specifically for people with disabilities
choices.textEs: Programas e instalaciones separados, diseñados específicamente para personas con discapacidad
choices.explanation: The act points the other way. Its aim is integration — the same jobs, the same buildings, the same services — and the regulations treat a separate programme as a last resort rather than as compliance.
choices.misconception: inverts an integration requirement into a requirement to separate

choices.text: Federal payments toward medical care and equipment for people with disabilities
choices.textEs: Pagos federales para atención médica y equipos para personas con discapacidad
choices.explanation: Those payments exist and come from elsewhere — Medicaid, Medicare and the Social Security disability programmes. This act creates rights against discrimination and appropriates no money for care.
choices.misconception: answers with the benefits programmes rather than the civil rights statute

choices.text: That every public school write and review an individualized education program for each eligible child with a disability in its district
choices.textEs: Que toda escuela pública redacte y revise un programa educativo individualizado para cada niño con discapacidad de su distrito que cumpla los requisitos
choices.explanation: That is a real and central requirement — of the other statute this standard names, the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. The two laws are routinely merged, and the distinction matters because one governs schooling and the other governs work and public life.
choices.misconception: assigns the education act's individualized program to the general access statute

choices.text: Reasonable accommodation for people with disabilities in employment, public services and public accommodations
choices.textEs: Ajustes razonables para personas con discapacidad en el empleo, los servicios públicos y los lugares de atención al público

items.dokRationale: Recall of what one statute requires. The student retrieves a provision; no reasoning about which constitutional clause a court relied on is involved. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that reasoning.
items.explanation: The act is a civil rights statute rather than a benefits programme: it does not pay for anything, it forbids exclusion. Its central device is reasonable accommodation — an employer or a business must make the adjustments that let a qualified person work or be served, up to the point of undue hardship, which is what makes it an equal-access law rather than a funding one.
items.explanationEs: La ley es un estatuto de derechos civiles y no un programa de prestaciones: no paga nada, prohíbe la exclusión. Su mecanismo central es el ajuste razonable: un empleador o un comercio debe hacer las adaptaciones que permitan a una persona cualificada trabajar o ser atendida, hasta el punto de la carga excesiva, y eso es lo que la convierte en una ley de igualdad de acceso y no de financiación.

items.stem: Before Congress passed the law now called the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, federal courts in 1972 had already ordered two school systems to educate children they had excluded. On what constitutional ground did those courts rule?
items.stemEs: Antes de que el Congreso aprobara la ley que hoy se llama Ley de Educación para Personas con Discapacidades, tribunales federales ya habían ordenado en 1972 a dos sistemas escolares educar a niños que habían excluido. ¿En qué fundamento constitucional se basaron esos tribunales?

choices.text: The Fourteenth Amendment's guarantees of equal protection and due process of law
choices.textEs: Las garantías de igualdad ante la ley y de debido proceso de la Decimocuarta Enmienda

choices.text: The Tenth Amendment, which reserves powers not given to the federal government to the states and the people
choices.textEs: La Decima Enmienda, que reserva a los estados y al pueblo los poderes no conferidos al gobierno federal
choices.explanation: A real provision, and it is the usual constitutional argument on the other side of this question: education is nowhere mentioned in the Constitution, so it is treated as a state responsibility. It is a limit on federal power, not a source of a child's right against a school district.
choices.misconception: offers the clause limiting federal power as the source of an individual right

choices.text: The Commerce Clause, which Congress used to reach private employers when it wrote the Americans with Disabilities Act
choices.textEs: La Cláusula de Comercio, que el Congreso usó para alcanzar a los empleadores privados al redactar la Ley de Estadounidenses con Discapacidades
choices.explanation: The second half is sound: reaching private businesses required the commerce power, because the Fourteenth Amendment restrains states rather than private parties. These two cases were against public school districts, which are state actors, so the Fourteenth Amendment applied directly.
choices.misconception: carries the clause needed to reach private parties into a case against a state actor

choices.text: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which bars discrimination in programmes that receive federal funds
choices.textEs: El Título VI de la Ley de Derechos Civiles de 1964, que prohíbe la discriminación en programas que reciben fondos federales
choices.explanation: A real provision, correctly described, and it covers race, colour and national origin. The funding statute that covers disability is Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 — a year after these cases, and itself part of the same sequence.
choices.misconception: names the funding-condition statute that covers a different protected class

items.dokRationale: The student must attach a line of cases to the constitutional provision that carried it, and reject three real provisions that govern neighbouring questions. Recalling when the education act passed is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: This is the sequence the standard is about: the courts moved first and Congress followed. Both 1972 decisions held that once a state provides public schooling it cannot exclude children with disabilities from it without violating equal protection, and cannot do so without notice and a hearing — due process. Congress then wrote those two holdings into a statute, which is why the law reads as it does: a right to an education, plus procedures parents can invoke.
items.explanationEs: Esta es la secuencia de la que trata el estándar: los tribunales se movieron primero y el Congreso siguió. Las dos decisiones de 1972 sostuvieron que, una vez que un estado ofrece escolarización pública, no puede excluir de ella a los niños con discapacidad sin violar la igualdad ante la ley, ni hacerlo sin notificación y audiencia, es decir, sin el debido proceso. El Congreso escribió luego esas dos conclusiones en una ley, y por eso la norma dice lo que dice: un derecho a la educación, más procedimientos que los padres pueden invocar.

items.stem: In Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) the Supreme Court held that states must license and recognise marriages between couples of the same sex. Which constitutional provision did the Court rely on?
items.stemEs: En Obergefell v. Hodges (2015), la Corte Suprema resolvió que los estados deben expedir licencias y reconocer los matrimonios entre parejas del mismo sexo. ¿En qué disposición constitucional se basó la Corte?

choices.text: The Full Faith and Credit Clause of Article IV, which requires each state to honour the public acts and records of the others
choices.textEs: La Cláusula de Entera Fe y Crédito del Artículo IV, que exige que cada estado honre los actos y registros públicos de los demás
choices.explanation: A real clause, correctly described, and it was genuinely argued in this area — it is the clause a claim to RECOGNITION of a marriage performed elsewhere would rest on. The Court decided the licensing question too, which that clause cannot reach.
choices.misconception: names the clause that would reach recognition between states but not licensing within one

choices.text: The Fourteenth Amendment, relying on both its Due Process Clause and its Equal Protection Clause
choices.textEs: La Decimocuarta Enmienda, apoyándose tanto en su Cláusula del Debido Proceso como en su Cláusula de Igualdad ante la Ley

choices.text: The Nineteenth Amendment, which forbids denying the vote on account of sex
choices.textEs: La Decimonovena Enmienda, que prohíbe negar el voto por razón de sexo
choices.explanation: A real amendment, ratified in 1920, and the only one that mentions sex. It governs voting and nothing else; its subject matter is the franchise rather than marriage or any other civil status.
choices.misconception: picks the one amendment that names sex without regard to what it governs

choices.text: An act of Congress passed in 2015 that recognised such marriages throughout the United States
choices.textEs: Una ley del Congreso aprobada en 2015 que reconocía esos matrimonios en todo Estados Unidos
choices.explanation: No such act passed in 2015; this was a court decision interpreting the Constitution, which is a different kind of act of government. Congress legislated in this area in 2022, seven years later, with a statute requiring interstate recognition.
choices.misconception: substitutes a statute for a constitutional holding, and dates it seven years early

items.dokRationale: The student must identify which of four real provisions a decision rested on, which requires knowing what each provision governs. Recalling the case's outcome or its year is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: The majority opinion rested on the Fourteenth Amendment and used both of its clauses: due process, on the ground that the liberty it protects includes certain personal choices central to individual dignity, and equal protection. Reading the two together follows the Court's own earlier marriage cases, and it is why the decision reached the licensing of marriages rather than only their recognition across state lines — which is what a different clause would have reached.
items.explanationEs: La opinión mayoritaria se basó en la Decimocuarta Enmienda y empleó sus dos cláusulas: el debido proceso, con el fundamento de que la libertad que protege incluye ciertas decisiones personales centrales para la dignidad individual, y la igualdad ante la ley. Leer ambas juntas sigue los propios casos anteriores de la Corte sobre el matrimonio, y por eso la decisión alcanzó la expedición de licencias y no solo su reconocimiento entre estados, que es lo que habría alcanzado otra cláusula.
